author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In US-blockaded Cuba, ingenious mechanics and inventors revive old machines to survive during a time of scarcity.

When the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, Cuba was plunged into crisis. Fuel, food and spare parts vanished almost overnight. This character-led documentary shows how common Cubans refused to give up – and instead built a new culture of radical repair. From Havana’s Malecon to small-town back yards, it follows mechanics, street vendors and a teacher-turned-inventor who live by one rule: “invent and resolve”.

A pristine US Plymouth Fury convertible of the 1950s hides a Soviet engine, Japanese gearbox and handmade parts; washing machines become coconut graters, solar dryers and tools for urban farms. Cuban historians and designer Ernesto Oroza reveal the philosophy behind this “technical disobedience”, treating every object as raw material to hack and extend. title: “Invent and resolve”: How Cuba's survived six decades of US blockade | Al Jazeera World Documentary

This episode follows former members of the national army accused of carrying out the so-called “falsos positivos” (false positives) — extrajudicial executions in which innocent civilians were executed, then falsely presented as combat casualties by the government as a way to bolster the numbers of enemies killed. Soldiers testified to their involvement in the assassinations to the families of the victims as part of the peace process. author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Conflicts, poverty and climate change are just some of the issues behind an unprecedented, global, displacement crisis.
Each year millions of people risk their lives in hopes of a better future, making treacherous journeys. 
Europe is among the destinations of a rising number of arrivals, often from Africa.
Thousands attempt to reach Europe mainly through the Central Mediterranean, Western Mediterranean and Western African routes. 
The Western Mediterranean route connects North Africa to mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands. 
As many countries move to curb migration, the Spanish government has approved plans to give half a million undocumented migrants legal status.  

Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque reports from the town of Belyounech, Morocco.

Andrew Geddes is a professor of migration studies at the European University Institute and the director of the Migration Policy Center.
He said European immigration policy has led to the emergence of more dangerous routes.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Ethan Baker, the mayor of Troy, Michigan and former Republican state House candidate, told Al Jazeera that Trump's State of the Union speech painted a mixed economic picture. 
He acknowledged falling inflation and stock market gains but noted residents still feel cost-of-living pressures. 
On tariffs, Baker supports the president's right to use them as a tool but warned they hit Michigan's auto industry hard. 
He observed Trump was more restrained on the issue than in recent days. 
Regarding immigration, Baker stressed public safety is his priority. 
He said the issue is complex, with some residents fearing federal enforcement while others see its value, and called for consensus reforms. 
On Republican election fears, Baker said Trump's speech had good moments but noted midterms are far off and much can change. 
Finally, on Iran, Baker praised rare bipartisan unity against Iran obtaining a nuclear weapon and suggested Trump's military buildup may be a bargaining tool for peace through
title: What Trump's speech means for midterms and Iran policy: Republican mayor shares his analysis

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
US President Donald Trump has touted his economic record during the longest State of the Union address in history, boasting that he had ushered in a “golden age”, as he sought to project an aura of success at a fraught moment for his presidency.
Trump did not offer more clarity regarding his plans for Iran, amid growing concern that he may be inching closer to a military conflict with the nation. “My preference is to solve this problem through diplomacy,” he said.
Trump took a moment to again target Somali Americans in Minnesota by labelling them “pirates”, and blamed unrestricted immigration for increased crime and rising economic costs for Americans.
Trump’s address comes amid economic uncertainty driven, in part, by his use of far-reaching tariffs, some of which were struck down by a Supreme Court ruling last week.

Al Jazeera’s Kimberly Halkett joins us live from Washington, DC to discuss this.
